chunks: Jibrīl عليه السلام descended upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, and he said to him: “O Jibrīl, admonish me.”
So he said: “O Muḥammad, live as you wish, for indeed you will die; love whomever you wish, for indeed you will part from him; and do whatever you wish, for indeed you will meet it.”
The honor of the believer is his salat (prayer) by night, and his dignity is in withholding harm from the people.

key_terms.صَلَاتُهُ بِاللَّيْلِ: His night salat (prayer); worship performed during the night.
key_terms.عِظْنِي: Admonish me; give me moral counsel and warning.
key_terms.كَفُّ الْأَذَى: Refraining from harm; withholding injury and offense.
key_terms.مَيِّتٌ: One who will surely die; mortal and destined for death.
key_terms.مُفَارِقُهُ: Parting from him; being separated from the one loved.
key_terms.مُلَاقِيهِ: Meeting it; encountering the result or consequence of one’s action.

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about death, deeds, night prayer, and avoiding harm to people?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a concise admonition about the certainty of death, separation from loved ones, and meeting the consequences of one’s deeds. It also teaches that a believer’s true honor is found in night salat (prayer) and true dignity in refraining from harming others.
